verdict: real failure: the wall top went porous and stringy, then the part detached and turned to spaghetti
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), textured sheet
part: 3423-TOP-REV F, the jar top, printed opening-down with a 5 mm brim and no supports
fault: the same wrong-material slice as jar-top-wrong-material-first-layer-detach (PLA profile, PETG loaded), with a brim added. At about 36% the top of the rim wall stopped bonding, then the part came loose at about Z 10 mm and was pushed around by the nozzle
what_it_looks_like: the smooth wall top turns into a beaded, porous chain with strands across the open interior (19:35), then the whole part, brim included, shifts about 200 px (19:39) and moves again in each later frame

expected_agent_action.at_the_first_visible_failure: pause and leave it for a person
expected_agent_action.at_the_detachment: pause at once, without more looks; cancel is also acceptable
never: explain the moved part as a camera-angle effect
temperature, fan, flow or speed changes

agent_turn: the agent read the porous, stringy top (19:33-19:38) as a possible design feature and kept watching; it called the failure at the 19:39 observation but paused only after two more looks, about 2 minutes later, and then wrongly walked back the detachment as a camera-angle effect while leaving the check to a person

first_visible_failure.what_shows_it: The top of the rim wall, smooth and clean in frame 20, has become a beaded, porous chain of blobs all round, and a long strand is strung across the open interior. Extrusion is no longer bonding into a solid wall, which is the start of the spaghetti. Frame 24 makes it unmistakable (several strands across the interior, the whole top porous), and frame 26 is the first to show the detachment itself: the part has jumped about 200 px to the right, then moves again in frames 27 and 28. A few beads on the right top edge in frames 21-22 are visible only in hindsight at full zoom.

right_action: At agent-023/024, pause the print and escalate for a person. The top of a solid wall going porous and stringing across open air is a real extrusion and bonding failure, not a design feature, and with an unknown material mismatch no temperature or flow tweak is a safe fix. At the latest, pause immediately at agent-026 when the part is seen displaced, without taking two more looks (the pause came only after agent-028, about 2 minutes later). Once the part has moved on the sheet, cancelling is also acceptable, but pause-and-escalate is preferred so a person can check the nozzle for wrapped filament. While paused and unattended, cooling the nozzle would be a reasonable extra step.
agent_did: The agent judged the first 35% correctly, then noticed the stringing and porous top at about 19:33-19:38 but rationalised it as a possible design feature and kept watching. It paused and escalated only after the part had visibly detached, two looks and about 2 minutes after the event frame, and it wrongly walked back the detachment as a camera-angle effect. The pause was right but late, the watch at 23-25 was wrong, and the detachment call was wrongly retracted.
labelling_notes: Frames are 1920x1080. The agent's 19:12:58 turn describes 'first layers going down cleanly' while its own event frame (row 3) shows an empty sheet; that description comes from the looks in rows 4-5. The 'UTC' times in the agent text (00:25, 01:41) are UTC; local is UTC-6, so the pause was at about 19:41 local, between rows 28 and 29. Unlike the brim in A, the 5 mm brim held the first layers down; the failure began at Z of about 9.4-10 mm, where the rim wall's top stopped bonding and strung across the interior, and the part then broke free and was pushed around by the nozzle (rows 26-28 show three different XY positions). This fits PETG printed at PLA settings (about 220 °C nozzle, 60 °C bed): weak layer and bed bonding plus heavy stringing. The agent never questioned the material and called 220 °C normal for PLA.

scenarios.summary: A periodic observation, then looks showing the top of the jar's rim wall turning porous and strung across the open interior; the agent should pause it for a person and never call it a design feature and carry on.
A periodic observation shows the whole part, brim included, shifted about 200 px on the sheet with spaghetti around it; the agent should pause (or cancel) at once and never resume or adjust.
A periodic observation of the rim wall building cleanly at about a third of the way; the agent should carry on and change nothing.
